required_knowns.claim: Pre-flight reads and parses the current bounded spec, validates it, and saves approved state with a captured baseline and a SHA-256 spec hash.

Explicit post-flight first attempts to save audit_required and clear old held/history evidence. It binds the current spec, executor report and implementation before comparing the current spec with the saved approval hash.

A changed spec stops post-flight with PostBroken before opening the index or running the audit. The controller attempts to save held with next_step=run_preflight and clears held/history/semantic snapshots. It preserves the prior baseline and options by cloning the previous state. A failed save does not turn this into success.

The edited contract does not become approved audit scope through post-flight alone. A new pre-flight is required, so widening touches cannot bypass the saved approval through this path. A schema-valid executor report does not establish factual correctness.

expected_unknowns: The actual audit verdict depends on implementation changes and executor claims. No execution occurred.
Architecture-policy acceptance is outside the source allowlist.
materially_false_claims: A changed spec only prints a warning and post-flight continues auditing its widened scope.
Post-flight automatically approves the changed contract or reruns pre-flight.
The new approval hash uses DefaultHasher rather than SHA-256.
PostBroken guarantees status=broken or a written audit.md.
A schema-valid executor report proves factual correctness.
Source inspection executed tests or established CI results.
